principle: Commercial Rent Stabilization memory must preserve the full attributed support chorus, legislative lineage, public-official speech, qualifications, and non-recoveries without converting alignment into endorsement or testimony into verified fact.

criteria.description: The collection distinguishes the municipal Int 1796 and Int 0093 bills from the current state-legislation resolution lineage.
Every legislation lifecycle statement is tied to an official Council record and dated status snapshot.
Prime-sponsor and co-sponsor stated-meeting records preserve full recovered turns, including honest procedural-only non-recoveries.
Public-official records distinguish direct bill support, support for related measures, problem recognition, and mechanism objections.
Every included supportive public-official statement is a complete attributed transcript turn or full official support document.
Opposition, unrelated remarks, agency non-endorsement, and missing transcript attachments remain visible in a coverage ledger.
The complete recovered oral support cohort and all attributed supportive or qualified-support written submissions are retained.
Direct support and qualified support remain distinct, and inclusion never implies agreement on every provision.
Direct emails, telephone numbers, postal boxes, and street addresses are removed from the public derivative corpus.
The official Council attachments remain canonical and testimony assertions are not presented as independently verified facts.
Generated data, source pages, and indexes are reproducible and freshness-checked.
Any later portfolio projection requires separate audience, claim, credit, and editorial review.
The active A5568A and S8319 records retain complete official sponsor memoranda, current committee status, prime sponsors, and verified co-sponsors.
Official written statements, sponsor memoranda, event transcripts, Council testimony, and corroborating interviews remain distinct source types.
Every included public-event speech is a complete timestamp-bound turn from a hash-bound transcript, with pre-event and unrelated room audio excluded through an explicit coverage ledger.
Shahana Hanif's late-2025 statement and Brad Lander's statement are retained with the public offices they held at that event.
Eon Huntley's March 2026 statement is attributed to him as an Assembly candidate, while his later primary victory is recorded only as later context.
A chamber-speech non-recovery remains visible while both state bills are in committee; no floor or introduction speech is inferred from a sponsor memorandum or press release.
